title: Operator sees costs in the CLI
description:
An operator running `auritus worker` on their own GPU is exactly the person
who wants to know what the cloud fallback is costing when their worker is
offline. Give them a cost command.

## Feature

```gherkin
Feature: Viewing costs from the command line

  Scenario: Operator sees a cost summary
    Given costs exist for the last thirty days
    When the operator runs "auritus cost"
    Then the total gpu cost is printed
    And the total platform cost is printed
    And the total avoided cost is printed

  Scenario: Operator scopes costs to a site
    Given costs exist for two sites
    When the operator runs "auritus cost --site" with one site
    Then only that site's costs are printed

  Scenario: Operator sees a daily breakdown
    Given costs exist for the last seven days
    When the operator runs "auritus cost --daily"
    Then one row is printed per day

  Scenario: Operator sees estimate against actual
    Given a reconciled day exists
    When the operator runs "auritus cost --daily"
    Then the estimated and actual cost are both printed for that day

  Scenario: Inspecting a job shows its cost
    Given a Batch job completed with a GPU cost
    When the operator runs "auritus job show" with its content hash
    Then the job gpu cost and billed seconds are printed

  Scenario: A locally processed job shows zero GPU cost and its avoided cost
    Given a local job completed
    When the operator runs "auritus job show" with its content hash
    Then the job gpu cost is zero
    And the job avoided cost is printed
```

## Implementation brief

**`cli/src/auritus/api.py`** -- `get_costs(site_id=None, from_date=None, to_date=None, daily=False)`
calling `GET /admin/costs`.

**`cli/src/auritus/commands/cost.py`** (new) -- a `cost` command group
following the shape of `commands/site.py`: catch `AuritusApiError`, print to
stderr in red, `raise typer.Exit(code=1) from exc`. Options `--site`,
`--daily`, `--from`, `--to`.

**`cli/src/auritus/cli.py`** -- `app.add_typer(cost_cmd.app, name="cost")`.

**`cli/src/auritus/commands/job.py`** -- extend `job show` output (from the
M10 story auritus-7d8ffa) with the cost attributes.

**Formatting** -- print dollar amounts to four decimal places, not two. A
single clip may cost a fraction of a cent, and rounding to cents renders most
per-job costs as `$0.00`, which is the exact failure this epic exists to fix.
Totals can round to cents.

**Label estimates as estimates.** Every figure here except the reconciled
actual is modelled. The output should say so once, plainly, rather than
presenting modelled dollars in the same voice as an invoice.

## Blocked on

The daily cost rollups story, for `GET /admin/costs`.
Job-level output additionally assumes the M10 CLI story (auritus-7d8ffa).

comments.author: home
comments.text: Implemented on feature/cli-costs, merged to develop. auritus cost (--site/--from/--to/--daily) prints GPU/platform/avoided cost as three separate labelled lines at 4 decimal places, plus a modelled-estimate disclaimer. job show now formats cost fields to 4 decimals and only shows avoided_cost_usd when its basis isn't 'batch_job'. Caught and fixed in review: the empty-result check was 'not total', but the real API always returns total populated with every field zeroed (summed from daily, never an empty dict) -- that check could never actually trigger, so a genuinely empty range would have printed a full zeroed-out summary instead of 'No cost data'. Fixed to check whether every total figure is actually zero; also had to reconcile with a pre-existing test that mocked an empty daily + nonzero total (impossible against the real API, since total is derived by summing daily) -- the corrected condition satisfies both realistic and that edge case. Independently re-verified: black/ruff, pytest (72 passed), behave (30 features, 116 scenarios).
